info.description:
FiestaBoard drives one or more split-flap displays from templated pages.

### Hello world

Put text on the board right now:

```bash
curl -X POST http://fiestaboard.local:4420/api/v1/boards/primary/message \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text": "HELLO WORLD"}'
```

`primary` works as a board id on every `/v1/boards/...` path, so a
single-board install never has to look one up — and a multi-board install
puts the id there instead.

### How the pieces fit

Four nouns, and one way to do each thing:

* A **board** is a physical display. `POST /v1/boards/{board}/message` writes
  to it; `GET /v1/boards/{board}` says what is on it and why.
* A **page** is a template: literal text plus `{{plugin_id.variable}}`
  placeholders that **plugins** fill with live data.
* A **schedule** (or a **collection**) decides which page a board shows at a
  given moment. A message write bypasses both for a one-off; `DELETE
  /v1/boards/{board}/message` hands the board back to the schedule.

### Base URL

nginx fronts the API under `/api`, so every path below is reached as
`/api/<path>` — `GET /v1/status` is
`http://fiestaboard.local:4420/api/v1/status`. These docs live at
`/api/docs`, the schema at `/api/openapi.json`.

### What is not here

This document is the API to build against: 33 operations. The app serves
~200 more, but they are the web UI's private RPC channel — undocumented on
purpose, with no compatibility promise, and liable to change in any release.
They are published separately at `/api/internal/openapi.json` for the UI's
own contract checks, and can be browsed at `/api/docs` by picking
**Internal web UI API** in the definition dropdown at the top of the page.
Two flat legacy operations, `POST /send-message` and `POST /refresh`,
remain here because earlier documentation named them; both
are deprecated and both name their `/v1` replacement in a `Link` header.

### Deprecated board fields

Since settings v4, a board's connection lives in its `output_config`, read
alongside its `output`. The flat connection fields that board responses
still carry (`api_mode`, `host`, `port`, `local_api_key`, `cloud_key`,
`note_array_token`, `tiles`, and the `board_api_mode`, `board_host` and
`board_key_set` summary fields) are copies of it, kept for compatibility
through v10 and removed in v11. Every response that carries them sends
`Deprecation: true` and a `Link` with `rel="deprecation"` pointing here,
and the schema marks the typed ones `deprecated`. The same fields leave the
MQTT `board_api_mode` entity and the MCP board tools in v11.

### Authentication

Off by default: a fresh install answers every request. With
`FIESTABOARD_AUTH_ENABLED=true`, a script sends
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` (create one with `POST /auth/mcp-token`),
which is accepted on every `/v1` path and on `/api/mcp`. The web UI instead
carries the session cookie that `POST /auth/login` sets.
info.title: FiestaBoard Display API

post.description:
Deprecated: use ``DELETE /v1/boards/{board}/message`` instead.

Manually trigger a display refresh.

Args:
    board_id: Optional board to refresh (query param, or
        ``{"board_id": ...}`` in the JSON body). Omitted → legacy
        behavior: refresh every board, primary first (issue #1244).

500.description: The server could not complete the operation. Deliberately raised, not an unhandled error.

post.description:
Deprecated: use ``POST /v1/boards/{board}/message`` instead.

Send a custom message to a board.

``board_id`` (optional) targets one board; omitted → the primary board,
which is what every caller got before this endpoint could address a
second one (issue #1247). Gate for gate this is the same policy the MCP
executor applies — see ``src/ops/executors.py``.

The v1 successor takes the board in the path, so it cannot be forgotten,
and reports whether flaps actually moved rather than only that the
request was accepted.

A silenced board (#1943, #1944): ``override_silence`` writes anyway;
otherwise the message is held (202, ``held: true``) when the board's
silence schedule holds messages until silence ends, and refused (409)
when it does not.

202.description: Held: the board is silenced and will show this when it ends.

409.description: Conflict — duplicate id, or a resource pinned by the environment.

429.description: Rate-limited — the request arrived inside a minimum interval; see Retry-After.

500.description: The server could not complete the operation. Deliberately raised, not an unhandled error.

get.description: Every configured board, with the id you use in the rest of this API, its grid size, and whether it is currently paused or following its schedule. The board marked `is_primary` is the one the literal path segment `primary` resolves to, so a single-board install never has to look an id up at all.
get.summary: List the boards this install drives

get.description: One answer to 'what is this board showing, and why'. It merges what the internal API splits across three endpoints: the flaps currently on the board, the page pinned to it by hand, and the page its schedule selects for right now. `source` says which of the two won. `board` may be a board id or the literal `primary`.
get.summary: Read a board and everything it is doing

patch.description: Rename a board, pause or resume it, turn its schedule on or off, choose whether FiestaBoard takes it back from another app (`auto_restore`), or set the page it falls back to when the schedule has a gap. Only the fields you send are applied; omit the rest. Pausing stops every write to the board from every code path — the display loop, schedules, plugin triggers, MQTT and this API alike.

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

put.description:
Sets the page (or collection) this board shows until something changes it — the sticky selection a schedule falls back from. The page is rendered and sent immediately. Send `null` to unpin, after which the board follows its schedule again. Pinning a page whose size does not match the board is rejected.

The selection is stored whether or not the send succeeded, so check `sent` — and `error`, which names the render or send failure when it is false.

While the board is silenced the page is pinned but not shown: `sent` is false, `silenced` is true and `reason` says when it will appear. Send `override_silence: true` to show it now anyway.

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

502.description: An upstream the server called on your behalf failed.

put.summary: Pin a page to a board

delete.description: Undoes a `POST` to this path. Any timed message is cancelled, the board's content cache is dropped, and the display loop re-renders whatever the schedule or the pinned page says should be there — which is a blank board when nothing is scheduled. `sent` reports whether that re-render reached the board.

500.description: The server could not complete the operation. Deliberately raised, not an unhandled error.

delete.summary: Clear a board and let its schedule take over

post.description:
The one way to write to a board. Send exactly one of `text` (word-wrapped for you), `lines` (one string per row), `characters` (a raw flap grid), `page_id` (render a saved page), `fill` (one flap code everywhere; 0 blanks the board), `plugin_id` (a plugin's live data, formatted the way the plugin displays itself) or `template` (one line per row with plugin variables like `{{weather.temperature}}` filled from live plugin data).

Add `duration_minutes` to make it temporary — it reverts to your schedule, a chosen page, or a blank board when the time is up. `board` may be a board id or the literal `primary`.

`sent` in the response tells you whether flaps actually moved. It is false, with a `reason`, when the install's output target is UI-only and when the board already showed this exact content. A board that is paused or inside its silence window refuses the write with 409 rather than lying about it. Send `if_paused: "preview"` to get a 200 instead for a paused board: `sent` is false, `reason` says the board is paused, and `characters` is what it would have shown. Nothing is written.

A write superseded by a newer write returns 409: its content did not reach the board. A silenced board is left alone. When its silence schedule holds messages (`show_queued_on_exit`) the write is accepted for later: 202, `sent: false`, `held: true`, and it shows when silence ends. Otherwise it is a 409. Send `override_silence: true` to write anyway. A board made of several devices (a local note array) that takes the write on only some of them answers 502, and `detail.failed_regions` names the cells that did not update; sending again retries only those.

202.description: Held: the board is silenced and will show this when it ends.

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

409.description: Conflict — duplicate id, or a resource pinned by the environment.

429.description: Rate-limited — the request arrived inside a minimum interval; see Retry-After.

500.description: The server could not complete the operation. Deliberately raised, not an unhandled error.

502.description: An upstream the server called on your behalf failed.

post.description:
Put a board back after another app or controller overwrote it; the web app's Restore button calls this. FiestaBoard remembers what it last sent each board and skips a send that would not change it, so after an outside write it believes the board is already up to date. This forgets that for this one board and runs its display pass, which writes whatever the schedule, timed message or pinned page says belongs there.

Restore changes no selection: a timed message keeps running and the pinned page stays pinned (a primary board with nothing pinned falls back to its first page, as the display loop always does). A paused or silenced board refuses with 409, and a UI-only install answers `sent: false`.

`sent` means the board accepted the write. No supported board reports what it actually displays, so `device_observed` is always false — look at the board to confirm.

409.description: Conflict — duplicate id, or a resource pinned by the environment.

500.description: The server could not complete the operation. Deliberately raised, not an unhandled error.

post.summary: Restore what a board should show

get.description: Every collection. A collection is a set of pages plus a rule for choosing between them — rotate on a timer, pick at random, or switch on the value of a template expression — and it can be used anywhere a page id can.

post.description: Saves a set of pages and how to choose between them. `selection_mode` is `time` (rotate every `time.interval_seconds`), `random`, or `variable` (evaluate `variable.rules` in order and show the first match). The generated id is prefixed `collection:` and is usable wherever a page id is.

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

delete.description: Removes an unreferenced collection, leaving its member pages untouched. Returns 409 with references to change first if a board selection, schedule, schedule default, silence setting, or temporary override still uses it. A refused deletion changes nothing.

409.description: Conflict — duplicate id, or a resource pinned by the environment.

412.description: Precondition failed — the resource changed since it was loaded. Reload before editing.

get.description: The collection with this id: its member page ids in order, its selection mode, and the config block for that mode — the rotation interval, or the expression rules that pick between the members.

put.description: Applies only the fields you send. Every page id in `page_ids` must exist, and a `variable` rule may only point at a page the collection contains.

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

412.description: Precondition failed — the resource changed since it was loaded. Reload before editing.

get.description: Every function usable inside `{{ }}` — conditionals, arithmetic, text and date helpers — with its signature and a one-line summary. This is the reference for writing a collection's `variable` rules as well as for page templates.
get.summary: List the functions a template expression can call

get.description: Answers 200 whenever the process is serving. `service_running` reports whether the display loop — the thing that actually drives the boards — is running, which is separate from the API being reachable.
get.summary: Check that the instance is up

get.description: Settings that belong to the install rather than to one board: whether the schedule is on and the install-wide page shown when the schedule has a gap. A board's own values are on `GET /v1/boards/{board}`.

patch.description: Turn the install's schedule on or off, or set the install-wide page shown when the schedule has a gap. Only the fields you send are applied; omit the rest. Send `default_page_id: null` to clear it. To change one board, use `PATCH /v1/boards/{board}`.

get.description: Every page saved on this install. A page is a reusable board layout — literal text, plugin variables, or rows composed from other sources — that a schedule, a collection or `POST /v1/boards/{board}/message` can refer to by id.

post.description: Saves a new page and answers with it, including the generated `id` you refer to it by. `type` picks how it is built: `template` for text with `{{variables}}`, `single` for one plugin's output, `composite` for rows drawn from several sources. `device_type` must match the boards you intend to show it on.

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

delete.description: Removes the page and replaces active selections on every board with a compatible page, creating a welcome page when needed. Returns 409 with references to change first if a collection, schedule, schedule default, silence setting, or temporary override still uses the page. A refused deletion changes nothing. The response reports whether any selection changed; its single replacement id prefers the primary board.

409.description: Conflict — duplicate id, or a resource pinned by the environment.

412.description: Precondition failed — the resource changed since it was loaded. Reload before editing.

get.description: The saved page with this id, exactly as stored — its type, its device size, its template or row configuration, and its per-page transition overrides. 404 when no page has this id.

put.description: Applies the fields you send and leaves the rest alone. The response carries the updated page plus `incompatible_references`: places that still point at this page — a board's schedule, a pinned selection — where your change has made the size no longer fit.

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

412.description: Precondition failed — the resource changed since it was loaded. Reload before editing.

get.description: Every plugin installed on this instance, whether or not it is switched on. A plugin is a data source — weather, transit, a stock ticker — that contributes template variables you can put on a page. `enabled` says whether it runs; `configured` says whether its required settings have been filled in.

Everything about one plugin: its manifest, the template variables it contributes and their maximum lengths, its settings schema, and its current configuration. Stored secrets come back masked as `***`; sending that value back in a `PATCH` leaves the stored secret untouched.

patch.description: One call for the three things you can do to a plugin. Send `enabled` to switch it on or off, `config` to replace its settings, or both — the settings are written first so a plugin is never enabled with a configuration you meant to replace. Answers with the plugin's full detail, secrets masked.

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

patch.summary: Enable, disable or configure a plugin

get.description: The plugin's latest fetch, in both forms the internal API served separately: `data` is the raw variable payload a template reads from, and `lines`/`text` are the board-ready rendering of it. `available` is false, with `error` set, when the plugin is disabled, unconfigured, or its source could not be reached — a 200, because that is the answer to the question asked. 404 means no such plugin is installed.

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

get.summary: Read what a plugin is currently reporting

post.description: The webhook target. A plugin that declares a `receive` handler accepts a JSON body here and updates what it reports without polling anything — the way to drive a board from a system FiestaBoard cannot reach out to. 405 means this plugin does not accept pushes.

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

405.description: The resource exists but does not implement this operation.

post.summary: Push data into a plugin from outside

post.description: Runs a template against the current data and gives you back the text, so you can see what a page would look like before you save it. Pass `board` — a board id or `primary` — to lay it out for that board's size, or `device_type` to lay it out for a hardware shape you have not configured a board for; without either, the template is rendered at the default flagship geometry. Nothing is written to any board.

parameters.description: Board id, or 'primary', whose geometry the template should be laid out for.
parameters.name: board

schema.description: Board id, or 'primary', whose geometry the template should be laid out for.
schema.title: Board

parameters.description: Board shape to lay the template out for, as an alternative to naming a board. Use this to preview a page whose device type no configured board has.
parameters.name: device_type

schema.description: Board shape to lay the template out for, as an alternative to naming a board. Use this to preview a page whose device type no configured board has.
schema.title: Device Type

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

post.summary: Render a template without saving or sending it

get.description: Every schedule entry, newest rules included. Pass `board_id` to narrow it to one board, or `*` for all boards at once. Each entry says which page shows between which times, on which days; the response also carries the fallback page and whether scheduling is switched on.

post.description: Adds a rule: show `page_id` from `start_time` to `end_time` on the days `day_pattern` selects. Times may also be relative to sunrise or sunset (`start_type`, `start_sun_offset`), and a rule may recur weekly, on a calendar date every year, or once. Omit `board_id` for the default board.

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

delete.description: Removes this schedule rule. The page it pointed at is untouched, and the board falls back to its remaining rules — or to its gap page when none of them match.

412.description: Precondition failed — the resource changed since it was loaded. Reload before editing.

get.description: The schedule entry with this id, plus `resolved_start_time` and `resolved_end_time` — the wall-clock times a sunrise- or sunset-relative rule works out to today.

put.description: Applies only the fields you send, so a partial update cannot silently clear the ones you left out. `warnings` reports rules that now overlap or leave a gap without failing the write.

400.description: Invalid request — the payload references something that does not exist or violates a rule.

412.description: Precondition failed — the resource changed since it was loaded. Reload before editing.

get.description: What the instance is doing: whether the display loop is running, a summary of the resolved configuration, and per board whether it has a working connection, whether it is paused, which page it is showing, why it failed to start if it did, and its output's summary of its connection settings (`output_status`: connected or not_configured).
get.summary: Read the display loop's state, board by board

get.description: The whole template vocabulary in one answer: the built-in variables, everything the installed plugins contribute, the colour and symbol names, and the filters you can apply. `max_lengths` gives the longest value each variable can render to, which is what you size a row against.
get.summary: List every name a template can use

tags.description:
The FiestaBoard API. Four nouns — board, page, schedule, plugin — and one way to do each thing.

Start here: `POST /v1/boards/primary/message` with `{"text": "HELLO"}` puts text on your board. `primary` works as a board id on every `/v1/boards/...` path, so a single-board install never needs to look one up.

Every write reports what actually happened rather than merely acknowledging the request: `sent` is true only when flaps moved, and a `reason` says why when they did not.
tags.name: v1

tags.description: The display loop itself: health, status, start/stop/refresh.
tags.name: service

tags.description: Write to a board out of band, and read back what is physically on it.
